title: Bioaccumulation
text: “There was hardly any damage done, and Janon-sama dealt with them mercifully, so it was resolved peacefully. Apparently, he even improved the treatment of human slaves somewhat because of it.”
“Wow, Elmelo-san’s foster parent sounds amazing.”
“…Yes. Though I feel tempted to press him about just how much he knows regarding my own foster parents, I think I’ll stay quiet on that matter.”
Elephant was looking at me, I say. Yay! Elephant—I believe in you, indeed.
“So that counts as good treatment, does it?”
Well, it seemed they engaged in hard labor without going so far as outright torment, indeed.
“That’s right. If someone has a nasty streak, there are cases where humans get incorporated into food-production devices as ingredients.”
“Hold on, that’s a pretty concerning thing to just drop in there. That doesn’t sound okay at all.”
“Ah, that’s the stuff that doesn’t taste very good…”
“I don’t think they’d ever serve that to Shield Hero-sama and company.”
“I’m genuinely curious now, though…”
“Voff, it’s in bad taste, so there isn’t much demand for it.”
Whatever could that mean, I wonder?
“Do you happen to know about it, Gaelion-chan? Motoyasu-kun, do you know?”
“Why does Rival come to mind first, Father, I say?”
“No, well, Gaelion-chan knows a lot about Shieldfreeden, right? So I figured maybe there’s something like that there too.”
“I wish you’d rely on me more, indeed!”
“Yes, yes, I know. So, Motoyasu-kun, do you know?”
“Hmm…”
Was there such a thing, I wonder?
“What could it be?”
“No idea.”
Rabbit Guy and Crocodile Guy didn’t seem to have any clue either, indeed. Something that comes up in Siltvelt, involving humans…
“You don’t mean turning humans into food ingredients, do you?”
“No, that’s not it.”
“Among the reincarnators, there are some who kill demi-humans and serve them as meat, but that’s not what you mean either?”
“Ugh… that sounds plausible, but— oh, but Melromarc doesn’t have anything like that either. Does Siltvelt have something like that? Using humans, I mean?”
“Some radical extremists do it as a performance, but humans are famously not very tasty.”
Panda turned her face away with an unpleasant look around then, indeed. Somehow her attitude suggested she had some personal experience with the matter.

“Well, humans don’t have much edible mass to begin with. Come to think of it, being omnivorous and near the top of the food chain means you’d accumulate a lot of toxins through bioaccumulation, and since we’re roughly humanoid too, eating human flesh regularly could probably cause some dangerous illnesses. That might be part of why Melromarc doesn’t have a culture of eating demi-humans either.”
Father answered smoothly, just like that, indeed.
“Well, either way, it seems like no weird ingredients are coming out, so that’s fine, I suppose.”
“Voff.”
“I think it depends on the specific thing, though.”
“True. Sometimes there’s something that makes you flinch. In that sense, I guess I’m used to Melromarc’s cuisine by now.”
“That part I get too, chalking it up to otherworldly cooking and all.”

Saying that, Father turned to look at me, indeed. Hmm… food made from a production device with humans incorporated into it, was it? I hadn’t asked in detail about Siltvelt cuisine, so I couldn’t say, indeed.
“I might have eaten it before without knowing, but I really can’t say, indeed.”
“Well, you wouldn’t be able to tell just by looking at the finished product. Some things are better left unknown.”
“Voff, don’t worry, they don’t make it here.”
Seemed there was no strange cuisine to worry about after all, indeed.

And so, amid all that, we entered the castle and made our way toward the bedrooms, indeed. Along the corridor, there were paintings lined up—portraits, perhaps of generations of past heads of the household, indeed. Unlike the earlier family portrait, these were individual portraits, one person each.
“Ooh.”
“Apparently these are portraits of past family heads.”
Wolf walked past them without much interest, indeed.
“These kind of look like they’re about to move—that’s a little scary.”
“I believe there was actually a monster like that, living in the basement of the magic academy in Faubrey, indeed.”
“A moving painting monster, huh…”
“This one doesn’t move.”
“Yeah. I know, but… still…”
And then, Father’s gaze stopped on one of the generational portraits, indeed.
“There’s a wolfman mixed in here who looks kind of like Keel-kun.”
Ah, indeed, he did stand out. There was a portrait of a dog-like wolfman resembling Keel, indeed. Apparently one popped up now and then, indeed.
“That’s right. There really is someone who looks like Keel-san here.”
“Ah… someone like this was actually a family head?”
“Apparently so. And the next generation after him, this person, is recorded as having been fierce and courageous.”
And the next one depicted was a wolfman who was remarkably muscular and manly, almost frightening in appearance, indeed—an image absolutely brimming with intensity, indeed.
“Isn’t this one, on the other hand, kind of a portrait of a beast ruled purely by instinct?”
“It’s recorded that he excelled in both scholarship and combat, and that he defeated humans who underestimated him based on his looks.”
“Huh… so despite looking like a muscle-brain, he was actually calm and clever.”
“Voff. Over here, there’s a small family portrait from that same era.”

There, depicted, was a fierce-looking, muscular wolfman tenderly holding a puppy-like demi-human who resembled Keel, indeed. The one who looked like Keel seemed to be sighing about something, indeed. He appeared to be far older than Keel herself, indeed. The whole portrait gave off the air of a family where someone simply couldn’t hold their head up against another, indeed.
“Quite the gap there. Is this meant to be a parent-child relationship? Would’ve been funny to bring Keel-kun here to see this.”
“Keel-san did say she thought Wolf was cool, so she might have been delighted.”
“Heh… Wolf, why don’t you take Keel as a bride? If someone resembling your ancestors is mixed in there, your standards of beauty must line up with hers too.”
“Fufu… Keel will surely cross the finish line with an inult.”

At Crocodile Guy’s words, Wolf answered with a snort of derision, indeed. There seemed to be some kind of verbal sparring match going on between them, indeed. Multiplying Keel was Luna-chan’s grand ambition, indeed.
“Wolf, are you interested in Keel-kun?”
“Voff, not at all. Keel is strictly a junior.”
“I see. Well, given the whole dog connection, I thought you two might make a good match, but if Wolf’s not interested, guess there’s nothing to be done about it.”
“Voff!”
Wolf declared with great force that she had no interest in Keel whatsoever, indeed.
“Wouldn’t someone like Keel-san being family head risk weakening the bloodline, or get them driven out or something?”
“There was some family strife, but from what I’ve looked into, it turned out that the child was so remarkable that they made her the head regardless.”

…Hm? Come to think of it, didn’t Ark say something about one of Keel’s children being born with an incredibly muscular build? Could this be a pattern that shows up with the Keel type? This might be safe to mention to Father, indeed.
“It seems that types like Keel apparently sometimes produce incredible children, indeed.”
“Huh… so that’s a characteristic of Keel-kun’s type, then.”
“Incidentally, Father. Apparently this is also a characteristic of Shield Heroes. All of Father’s children turned out amazing, indeed.”
Even I could still recall Older Sister’s and Panda’s children even now, indeed. Father’s expression suddenly went rigid, indeed.
“Hey, Spear Hero.”
“That’s a bit too raw a topic.”
“But this is from my loop knowledge, indeed. Older Sister’s and Panda’s children were positively bursting with energy, and this is a story told about Shield Hero in Siltvelt, indeed.”
There had indeed been the sight of them thumping and asserting themselves inside Older Sister’s and the others’ bellies, indeed.
“Ah? I’m getting dragged into this conversation now?”

Panda, who had silently been carrying the baggage, furrowed her brow with some displeasure, indeed. Elephant had already gone ahead to the guest building, indeed. Incidentally, Panda’s subordinates were with her too. Some of them, apparently unused to a place as lofty as Wolf’s household, were looking around with expressions of astonishment. Indeed, some wolfmen were present among them—lower-ranking wolfmen, by the look of it.
“Well… if it keeps Siltvelt’s people from scheming something strange behind the scenes, then I suppose it’s fine for you, Larsazusa, to let Shield Hero gain some experience.”
“Why the hell are you all talking like that Spear Hero over there! Ugh, seriously, our parents came here with such high expectations, and it’s a huge pain!”
“I’m trying to make sure there’s no misunderstanding with Imiya either. Talk it through properly and decide for yourselves.”
“Hold on? I’d appreciate it if you didn’t decide things on your own, thanks?”

“But this is an issue we can’t avoid forever, isn’t it? Given the moves coming from Siltvelt. No matter how much we act as your escorts, you still need to gain some experience with this, at least to some degree.”
“…Even Shion is saying it now. I feel like I could be gentle with Keel-kun later…”
Oh my? Father’s eyes seemed to be gazing off somewhere very far away, indeed.
